newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields dip as Fed holds steady.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields dip as Fed holds steady.

text.p: *Australian bonds were lower in early trading, taking their cue from a rally from U.S. Treasuries after Tuesday's FOMC meeting left monetary policy unchanged.
Australian bond yields were lower in early trading, taking their cue from a rally from U.S. Treasuries after Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting left monetary policy unchanged.

June 10-year bond futures rushed to their highest level since February in after hours trading, but since then the market has wound back some of that move with the U.S. interest rate outlook still far from clear, analysts said.
"People think they (the Fed) still have to move in July, or maybe in August. It really leaves things in limbo," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.
"You can't actually buy the U.S. on the basis that the March tightening in (U.S.) policy was the last," Roberts added.
He felt that the Fed's stance will only have a minor, short-term impact on the local market, which will be otherwise engrossed with wages data over the next two days.

The Department of Industrial Relations will release it latest report on enterprise bargaining agreements (EBAs) at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), while final first quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings are due on Thursday.
The DIR report is expected to be a carbon copy of HSBC markets wages report earlier this week.
This report showed private sector agreements running at 4.9 percent in the March quarter from 4.4 percent in December.

The final AWOTE data will contain the private/public sector spilt and analysts will be looking for a private outcome of below 1.0 percent for annual growth of 3.5 percent to keep hopes, albeit slim, of a further policy easing.
The preliminary AWOTE showed an overall rise of 1.3 percent for annual growth of 4.6 percent.

Local yield differentials to the U.S. were little changed, while the market was outperformed by Canadaian debt, which rallied strongly against the U.S. on the Fed's unchanged policy. The short end of the New Zealand market remained under pressure on a weakening N.Z. TWI.
The 10-year bond contract struck 92.405 and its highest level since February in SYCOM trade, just short of anticipated resistance at 92.410.
